Hi Maya —

Thanks — attaching a short summary (reserved_options_summary.pdf) and an example SOW extract. High-level options below; I kept them intentionally prescriptive so procurement can pick a path. Karthik and Grace are looped for operational and pricing notes.

Option A — Conservative reserve (recommended for predictable latency):
- Cluster: 4 x A100 80GB (multi-tenant within your Dedicated pool)
- Min GPUs guaranteed: 16 (kept warm, KV cache persisted across sessions)
- Onboarding ramp: 16 -> 32 (week 1 -> week 6) with a weekly activation checkpoint
- Escape hatch: automatic 30% burn-credit refund if average utilization < 25% over first 60 days

Option B — Growth ladder (lower initial commitment):
- Cluster: 2 x A100 80GB + 4 x A40 (mixed footprint)
- Min GPUs guaranteed: 8 initially, 24 target by month 3
- Ramp schedule: step-up at month 1 and month 2; warm-sprint windows for peak days
- Soft fallback: ability to overflow to pay-as-you-go hosted models at 1.4x per-token premium

Option C — Aggressive throughput (for heavy burst + throughput SLAs):
- Cluster: 6 x A100 80GB dedicated (isolated pool)
- Min GPUs guaranteed: 24
- Ramp: activation in two waves (12 GPUs day 1, remainder day 14)
- Escape hatch: decommit window at month 6 with 90-day wind-down credits

Key operational notes:
- Warm cache: we persist KV caches across warm-start nodes for options A/C; Option B uses shorter cache retention to reduce cost.
- Autoscale & burst: each plan includes configured burst pool (up to 20% of committed GPUs) for short peak events; burst billing is metered separately.
- Metrics: we’ll provide a per-token latency & cost breakdown during onboarding and 2-weekly cadence thereafter.

Next steps: 1) confirm which option your procurement prefers 2) we send a tailored SOW and a proposed invoice cadence (monthly/quarterly) 3) schedule a 30-min ops sync with Karthik.

Maya / team —

Quick tech notes to help procurement understand the tradeoffs:
- Min GPUs = warm nodes that maintain model weights & KV cache. For sequence-heavy workloads (you reported avg seq 1.2k tokens) the sweet spot for latency is >=16 A100s. Below that you’ll see tail latency variance under 95th percentile SLA.
- Mixed fleets (A100 + A40) reduce cost but increase routing complexity; we recommend pinning critical low-latency routes to A100 subset.
- Ramp checkpoints should include a token-quality smoke test (we can provide an eval harness) and an inference-cost cap to avoid surprise spend during early traffic surges.
- Escape hatch mechanics we typically propose:
  1) First 60 days: utilization assessment with 30% credit if below threshold
  2) At 6 months: one-time decommit window with pro-rated credits over 90-day wind-down

Operational ask from ClearSail: please provide 2 weeks of traffic traces (anonymized) so we can map the activation pacing to realistic request concurrency and provide a burst plan.

Happy to run the ops sync once you send the traces.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
